name: 1834 Prairie Avenue (the Jones house): the brick barn on the alley, K12

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft's claim, kept: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Robinson's 1886 plate 10, which dates the 1600 and 1700 blocks' stables, stops at 18th Street, and nothing else read dates this one, so the range claims the 1904 target and no more. TO is the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the stable's alley (west) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 28 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_28.jpg) at pixel (570.42, 3314.63): the alley wall's line, read by median darkness profile at rows 3180-3220, 3330-3370 and 3420-3460 (571.67, 569.98, 569.11; the raster leans about 0.6 degrees, so the line is fitted through the three), halfway between the building's north and south wall lines (3153.15 and 3476.11). Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_28_gcps.json): local E 1339.172, N -3325.332, 0.25 m north of the middle of parcel prairie_1834's rear line, plus the datum origin. The bearing is the parcel's own (its north and south lines run at 0.616 degrees north of east), so the building's ends lie along the lot lines.
placement.symbolic_location: 1834 S. Prairie Avenue: west side of Prairie between 18th and 20th Streets, parcel prairie_1834 (data/street_grid/1904.json), the lot south of 1828; on the rear lot line, its alley wall on the east line of the alley between Indiana and Prairie.

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the stable from the alley line (pixel column 570.42 at its middle row; the line read by median darkness profile at rows 3180-3220, 3330-3370 and 3420-3460 as 571.67, 569.98 and 569.11, the raster leaning about 0.6 degrees) to its east wall line (718.64 and 717.85 at the lower two of those rows), 7.52 m deep, and from its north wall line (row 3153.15, the line it shares with 1828's building, which the sheet draws once) to its south one (3476.11), 322.96 pixels at the sheet's 0.050558 m a pixel, 16.33 m along the alley. Against the north 7.89 m of its east wall (to the piece's south wall line, row 3309.10) it draws a one-storey brick piece out to an east wall line at column 780.53 (780.56 and 780.49 at rows 3180-3220 and 3260-3300), 3.09 m beyond the stable's (719.38 there). South of the stable an open strip about 3.6 m wide runs to the frame shed on the strip between 1834 and 1900 (row 3547.89). The kit's party wall stands inside this outline at the north end, its returns 0.5 m past the eaves, which is the kit's and not the sheet's; 1828's own building is still the district draft's.

stories.note: '2' lettered in the stable's north-west corner and '1' in the piece against its yard wall: two storeys and one. Built as the kit's carriage room (3.6 m) under a loft whose walls rise 2.7 m more to the eave, under the kit's 40-degree roof (3.15 m from eave to ridge over the 7.52 m span), and the piece as the kit's lean-to, 3.9 m high against the yard wall; those heights are RECONSTRUCTED. No dormer: the sheet draws none and the kit builds none.

construction.note: Stable and piece both drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '8' over '8' (inches) inside the stable's south wall; the '12 8' written across its north wall line stands on the line it shares with 1828's building and is not taken as this wall's.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick and the one window mark is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1834-stable-1935. The sheet gives the outline of the stable and of the one-storey piece against its yard wall at the north end, '2' and '1' storeys, the brick, and one of the key's window marks on the alley wall, a cross with a dot for each storey (the sign 1816's and 1824's alley walls carry), 7.87 m from the north wall (row 3308.72). It draws no fire-wall sign at either end. The kit stands its one party wall at the north end, on the lot line, where the sheet draws one wall against 1828's building, and its open gable at the south end, over the open strip. The mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s counts from the party wall's inner face, 0.33 m in, on the alley wall, and from the gable end on the yard wall). The rest of the alley wall is the kit's laid out for 16.3 m: two carriage bays 3.0 m clear, the loft hatch and hoist over the northern one and a loft sash over the other, a man door between the northern bay and the mark, and a stable sash and loft sash toward the south end. The yard wall, south of the one-storey piece, has two stable sash with loft sash over them and a door onto the workyard where the walk to the house meets it. The one-storey piece is built on the kit's lean-to fitting, standing on the lot line against the party wall as 1730's does (T-1932): 7.89 m along the yard wall, 3.09 m deep, its single-pitch roof rising to 3.9 m where it dies into the yard wall; a stable (Dutch) door and a sash in its front, both the kit's. The sheet breaks the wall line between the piece and the stable over about 1.5 m (2.85 to 4.32 m from the north wall), an opening between the two inside; it is not built, since the piece covers it. The kit's 40-degree gable runs its ridge along the alley, 3.15 m from eave to ridge over the 7.52 m span, with no dormer. The workyard is paved from the yard door 13.66 m east to the west face of the house's rear porch (sheet column 988.37, rows 3276.22-3357.89, drawn yellow and lettered OPEN 1st IR.CL.2nd), the walk 0.8 m south of the building's middle, inside the porch's width. Not built: the solid dot inside the piece (the key's vertical steam boiler; the kit has no stack and the sheet draws none) and a small cross inside the stable's south-west corner, which 1630's shed record reads as the key's shingle-roof sign: if it is, the kit's slate is wrong here, and the liberty says so.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof, party wall, lean-to heights and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot, and RECONSTRUCTED except where the window mark places a sash. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: Sheet 28 of the 1911 Sanborn letters the brick building two storeys high on the alley behind 1834 BARN, the sheet's word for a stable. The T-1841 sheet census (row s28-1834-rear) backcasts the building to 1904, and this record builds it as the house's stable and coach house: two carriage bays, a loft hatch with its hoist, stable sash, and no motor-garage part. INFERRED from the 1911 label carried back to 1904; no source read names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 28.
what_it_supplies: The water's edge beside the Illinois Central from about 40 m north of 18th Street to about 80 m south of it, and the easternmost track on to the paper's edge, as of 1911
The 1800 Prairie lot and the Glessner House footprint (stone, courtyard plan) as of 1911, and every Prairie- and Calumet-facing footprint from 18th to 20th Street
Its own printed Scale of Feet
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
The lake edge beyond the stretch the sheet actually inks: the pen line stops while the tracks run on

research_note: T-1935 refines the district draft (T-2329) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit, the third of the package's seven alley buildings on the west side of Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th, after 1816's and 1824's. The sheet census (census row s28-1834-rear, trace s28fp-1834-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. Read afresh off the committed sheet 28 raster by median darkness profiles rather than taken from the draft's fitted rectangles: the sheet draws a stable 7.52 m deep and 16.33 m along the alley on the alley line, its north wall on the line it shares with 1828's building, and a one-storey brick piece 3.09 m deep against the north 7.89 m of its yard wall. Robinson's 1886 atlas (plate 10) stops at 18th Street, so nothing read here dates the building before 1911. The one picture the T-1935 image gate names for it (Clark's c. 1905 street view north from 1936) shows the house fronts on Prairie Avenue and not the alley.
